entries.name: mcp
entries.reason: reports mcp_requests_total{outcome}, mcp_tool_calls_total{tool,outcome}, mcp_auth_failures_total{reason}, mcp_tool_call_duration_seconds{tool}, mcp_key_fetches_total{outcome}, mcp_issuer_up (the IssuerProbe, once a minute) and, for a call past the endpoint's limit per account, motorfix_rate_limit_refusals_total{route="POST /mcp"}, one McpToolCall log line per tool call and an mcp.tool <name> span; a new assistant grant is an audit row and an assistant_grant.created event

entries.name: web-e2e
entries.reason: test project, not deployed

entries.name: keycloak
entries.reason: staging only; health at /realms/master, answering once the realm is imported; Keycloak sends no telemetry itself: the worker reads its management /metrics (port 9000, private network) at KEYCLOAK_METRICS_URL once a minute into motorfix_keycloak_heap_used_bytes, motorfix_keycloak_heap_max_bytes and motorfix_datastore_up{store="keycloak"} on the overview dashboard's keycloak row, which fire keycloak-memory; the MCP server's mcp_issuer_up probe still fires mcp-issuer-unreachable

entries.name: mcp
entries.reason: staging only; health at /health/live; mcp_issuer_up is its liveness series

entries.name: insights
entries.reason: four nightly jobs, platform-daily, response-stats, profile-views and demand-daily, counted by motorfix_jobs_total{job_name,outcome} and logged once on their final failure; a missed night of the first two leaves the last figures in place and the next night recounts; demand-daily logs the days it wrote, and a missed night is caught up by the next, the read counting an unwritten day live meanwhile, then ranks every active brand by its searches over the 30 closed days and logs the ranked and changed counts, a failed ranking failing the attempt and leaving the previous ranks; profile-views has its own final-failure alert, since its counters expire two days after their day

entries.name: status-checks
entries.reason: one job every 30 seconds probes the admin dashboard's six service tiles and stores them in status_tile, counted by motorfix_jobs_total{job_name,outcome} and logged once on its final failure; a confirmed tile change logs 'StatusChecks <tile> <state> <figures>' and writes status_tile.changed; a failed run is not retried, the next one follows in 30 seconds; the tiles' own alerting is a later story

entries.name: system-log
entries.reason: the system_log_entry table's purge: one scheduler, system-log-purge, at 03:30 Europe/Bucharest deletes system log entries older than 90 days, counted by motorfix_jobs_total{job_name,outcome}, logging the rows deleted and once on its final failure, which worker-jobs-failed alerts; each new entry also publishes system_log.added to the admin live channel straight to Redis, a failed publish logging one SystemLog warning

entries.name: retention
entries.reason: the nightly retention job: one scheduler, retention-nightly, at 04:00 Europe/Bucharest deletes expired sign-in, phone-change, account and refresh tokens and sent invites, notifications past 12 months and legal documents (with their page files) of garages closed 5 years, and anonymises audit entries past their owner's closure; counted by motorfix_jobs_total{job_name,outcome}, one log line per kind with its count and one with the run's duration, a failed sweep failing the job (3 tries) and worker-jobs-failed on the last; worker-jobs-failed (reason overdue) fires when no run completed in 48 hours

entries.name: motorfix_rate_limit_refusals_total
entries.reason: counts every call refused past a rate limit (the route limits of rate-limit.config.ts and the existing ones alike) by method and route template only, 'unknown' when no route matched, never an address, account or e-mail; the api counts its 429s in ProblemFilter, the MCP its own as 'POST /mcp' (panel on motorfix-mcp too); a refusal logs nothing, and Redis down logs one warning per limit and admits the call

entries.name: motorfix_static_map_renders_total
entries.reason: counts every static map answer by outcome ok, invalid or tiles_failed, never a centre or an address, and times each render in motorfix_static_map_render_duration_seconds (0.25 to 5 s); tiles_failed above 5% of 20 renders in 10 minutes is folded into api-error-rate, keeping the alert count at 50

entries.name: motorfix_live_replays_total
entries.reason: counts every replay a returning live stream asked for (Last-Event-ID or ?since=) by outcome none, some or capped (200 rows), never an account; a capped rate is clients away long enough to miss more than a page, which the views' re-read covers; a failed replay read logs one Live warning and the stream goes on live, the database being down already alerted by postgres-unreachable and api-error-rate

entries.name: motorfix_live_replayed_rows_total
entries.reason: counts the notifications written by live replays, charted beside motorfix_live_replays_total on the same panel; a count has no failure of its own to alert on

entries.name: motorfix_live_stream_closes_total
entries.reason: counts every live stream the server ended by reason (expired, evicted, shutdown, reconnect, the planned close before Railway's 15-minute HTTP limit); an evicted surge is a client opening too many streams, which the one-stream-per-browser lock prevents, so it is watched on the panel, not paged

entries.name: motorfix_verification_presence_total
entries.reason: counts verification file presence entries created and removed and every presence store call that failed (store_unavailable), never an account or a file; a failure costs only the banner of who else has the file open, the file opens and decides as before, and an unreachable Valkey already pages through redis-unreachable

entries.name: motorfix_system_log_entries_total
entries.reason: counts every system status log write by kind and outcome (written, grouped, dropped), charted per hour and per day by outcome on motorfix-product, with one SystemLog error line per dropped entry naming only its kind and source; a dropped rate is the database being down, which postgres-unreachable and api-error-rate already alert

entries.name: reminders
entries.reason: its 09:00 Europe/Bucharest daily job also runs the listing draft sweep and the RAR re-check count, which tells every admin once a day through ADMIN_RECHECK_DUE and logs one RecheckDue line per run; since ST-68 the same daily job runs the yearly documents compliance step before the RAR re-check: it sends DOCUMENT_DUE at 30, 7 and 0 days and turns a cycle overdue the day after its due date with DOCUMENT_OVERDUE (both always e-mail and push), writes document.due and document.overdue events, counts motorfix_document_cycle_total{step} and refreshes the motorfix_documents_overdue gauge, logs one DocumentCycle line per run (day, reminders per stage, cycles turned overdue) and one on its final failure; shown on the worker dashboard's Documente anuale panel; a failed run fires worker-jobs-failed within 15 minutes, as any reminders job does

entries.name: review-posted
entries.reason: counted by motorfix_review_announced_total (built, muted, skipped) on motorfix-product, with one ReviewPosted log line per event naming the review id; BullMQ's queue metrics cover depth and failures

entries.name: verification-result
entries.reason: counted by motorfix_verification_result_total (built, skipped) on motorfix-queues; one VerificationResult log line per event with the file id, the decision and the owners told, and one for a sending (ST-301) with the number of admins told (the counter counts decisions only); the job runs in the worker's queue span; BullMQ's queue metrics cover depth, and the alert fires on a job's final failure

entries.name: garage-suspended
entries.reason: counted by motorfix_garage_suspended_notices_total (built, skipped) on motorfix-queues; one GarageSuspended log line per event with the garage id, the cause and the owners told, never the reason; the job runs in the worker's queue span; BullMQ's queue metrics cover depth, and the shared backlog and failed-job rules alert on it

entries.name: garage-restored
entries.reason: counted by motorfix_garage_restored_notices_total (built, skipped) on motorfix-queues; one GarageRestored log line per event with the garage id and the owners told, never the admin's note; the job runs in the worker's queue span; BullMQ's queue metrics cover depth, and the shared backlog and failed-job rules alert on it

entries.name: catalogue-job-pending
entries.reason: one ADMIN_CATALOGUE_JOB_PENDING per active admin for each catalogue_job.proposed event, keyed by the event id; one log line per event with the job id and how many admins were told, never a name; no counter of its own, as the admins' verification-queued notice has none: the notifications table holds what was built; the job runs in the worker's queue span; BullMQ's queue metrics on motorfix-queues cover depth, and the shared backlog and failed-job rules alert on a job that fails for good

entries.name: catalogue-job-decided
entries.reason: one CATALOGUE_JOB_DECIDED to the proposing garage's owner for each catalogue_job.decided event, keyed by the event id; one log line per event with the job id, the decision and how many owners were told, never the reason; no counter of its own, as its pending twin has none: the notifications table holds what was built; the job runs in the worker's queue span; BullMQ's queue metrics on motorfix-queues cover depth, and the shared backlog and failed-job rules alert on a job that fails for good

entries.name: admin-brands
entries.reason: the admin's brand list with its counts, the add and the edit (rename, retire, bring back), written to PostgreSQL with their audit entries in one transaction, then the cached active list dropped by bumping brands:version; one Brands log line per write naming the brand id and the admin's account id, never the name; a failed cache drop is a warning line; a 409 brand_exists or stale_value is the rule working; the API error-rate and latency rules cover the routes; no outside call

entries.name: document-refused
entries.reason: one DOCUMENT_REFUSED per garage owner for each document.refused event, keyed by the event id; one log line per event with the document and garage ids and how many owners were told, never a name or the note; no counter of its own: the notifications table holds what was built; the job runs in the worker's queue span; BullMQ's queue metrics on motorfix-queues cover depth, and the shared backlog and failed-job rules alert on a job that fails for good

entries.name: garage-report-decided
entries.reason: counted by motorfix_garage_report_decided_notices_total (built, skipped) on motorfix-queues; one log line per event with the garage id, the decision and how many reporters were told, never a name, the note or the reason; the job runs in the worker's queue span; BullMQ's queue metrics cover depth, and the shared backlog and failed-job rules alert on a job that fails for good

entries.name: quote-accepted
entries.reason: one QuoteAccepted log line per job naming the quote id and how many staff were told, or why none; BullMQ's queue metrics cover depth and failures; the acceptances themselves are counted by motorfix_quote_accepts_total

entries.name: quote-declined
entries.reason: one QuoteDeclined log line per job naming the quote id and how many staff were told, or why none; BullMQ's queue metrics cover depth and failures; the declines themselves are counted by motorfix_quote_declines_total

entries.name: quote-received
entries.reason: counted by motorfix_quote_received_total (built, muted) on motorfix-queues and motorfix-product; BullMQ's queue metrics cover depth and failures

entries.name: quote-timers
entries.reason: carries the relay's request.declined events and each decline's undo-window timer and sweep; counted by motorfix_decline_windows_closed_total (sent, muted, skipped_undone, skipped_closed, already_told, by timer or sweep) with one DeclineWindow log line per window naming the recipient id; BullMQ's queue metrics cover depth and failures; decline-window-sweep-late fires when the sweep closes more than 10 windows in an hour (lost timers)

entries.name: brevo
entries.reason: carries e-mail and the WhatsApp sign-in and phone-change codes (ST-139: sent straight from the API, a failure logs 'phone code not sent: whatsapp_failed (<kind>)' and counts on the request-duration metric as the sign-in's 502 or the phone change's 503 send_failed, which api-error-rate covers); worker-jobs-failed and worker-saturation cover the worker's e-mail sends

entries.name: s3
entries.reason: the app's object store; the worker's status checks also list the nightly backup bucket with their own client (libs/domain/src/status/probes/probes.ts, BACKUP_S3_*, ST-294), a failed listing showing the backup tile red with its reason

entries.name: geoapify
entries.reason: reports motorfix_places_lookups_total{provider,outcome} and motorfix_places_provider_duration_seconds{provider}

entries.name: public-web
entries.reason: the status checks call the public web address every 30 seconds (/health/ready, the popular brands and one garage search without the log flag), timed on the Outside calls row (http_client_request_duration_seconds by server_address); a failed probe shows its tile red, the tiles' own alerting is a later story

entries.name: openfreemap
entries.reason: map tiles: the browser fetches them for the interactive maps, no key, a failed load showing the map-down message; the api's static map (libs/domain/src/maps/static-map/static-map.renderer.ts) reads the TileJSON once an hour and up to a few tiles per image, each a static-map.tile span and an Outside calls row entry, 2 s a tile and 5 s an image, a failure counted as motorfix_static_map_renders_total{outcome=tiles_failed} under api-error-rate

entries.name: onrc-portal
entries.reason: a link the admin opens in a new tab to look a company up by hand; neither the browser app nor the API calls it, and the check the admin records is counted by motorfix_verification_checks_total

entries.name: anaf-company-lookup
entries.reason: a link the admin opens in a new tab to look a CUI up by hand; neither the browser app nor the API calls it, and the check the admin records is counted by motorfix_verification_checks_total

entries.name: rar-portal
entries.reason: a link the admin opens in a new tab to look a RAR number up by hand; neither the browser app nor the API calls it, and the check the admin records is counted by motorfix_verification_checks_total

entries.name: motorfix_maintenance_refusals_total
entries.reason: counts calls refused while maintenance is on, by route and role (visitor or signed_in); ST-879 adds the dashboard; a count has no failure to alert on; the api-error-rate rule covers the service that reports it

entries.name: motorfix_platform_rule_changes_total
entries.reason: counts rule change requests by action (requested, approved, refused, cancelled), with one PlatformRuleChanges log line per step; a count has no failure to alert on; the api-error-rate rule covers the service that reports it

entries.name: motorfix_copy_voice_changes_total
entries.reason: counts copy voices switched on, off, pinned or unpinned by admins, with one CopyVoices log line per changed voice; a count has no failure to alert on; the api-error-rate rule covers the service that reports it

entries.name: grafana-faro
entries.reason: the browser's collector; besides the web vitals and errors it receives the prefetch measurement (context path profile, outcome fetched, cancelled, hit, expired or skipped, and a fetch's duration), shown on the web-vitals dashboard's pre-fetch panel; since ST-1191 also the upload measurement (context purpose garage_photo or legal_document, outcome queued, resumed, sent or failed, and a sent upload's duration from its first attempt; no file name, draft id or key), shown on the uploads panel; since ST-947, under analytics consent only, a per-tab session id and the journey events session_start, session_resume and view_changed (route templates), so Frontend Observability lists sessions and route walks

entries.name: keycloak
entries.reason: the identity server signing-key fetch, host read from ASSISTANT_ISSUER; counted in mcp_key_fetches_total{outcome} on the mcp dashboard; a failed fetch fires mcp-key-fetch-failures, and calls answer 503 (not counted as sign-in failures); the IssuerProbe reads its discovery document once a minute into mcp_issuer_up, which fires mcp-issuer-unreachable

entries.name: plausible
entries.reason: only the visitor's browser calls it, and only after a valid Accept; nothing on the server waits on it, Plausible's own site shows the page views, and the consent choices it rests on are counted on motorfix-product (motorfix_consent_records_total)

entries.name: mcp_tool_calls_total{tool=~"list_quote_requests|get_schedule|get_day_sheet|get_stats|decline_quote_request"}
entries.reason: the four garage read tools count under mcp_tool_calls_total{tool,outcome} and mcp_tool_call_duration_seconds{tool}, one McpToolCall log line and an mcp.tool <name> span per call, like every tool; the existing mcp-tool-errors alert sums every tool; reads write no audit row; decline_quote_request (ST-345) acts, so its decline writes the audit row marked via the assistant and counts in motorfix_request_declines_total

entries.name: motorfix_cache_total
entries.reason: counts each cached read (profile, home, popular-brands, brands (whether a brand slug a profile read names is in the catalogue), and the pre-fetched driver-home and garage-home lists) by outcome: hit, miss, stale (served past its soft expiry), coalesced (a concurrent read served by another read's call), negative (a remembered not-found or empty answer), fallback (Redis failed and PostgreSQL answered), warm (filled by the post-deploy warm-up or, for driver-home and garage-home, by a sign-in), and purge (an entry removed by a tag purge, from the worker); one warn log line when Redis first fails and one when it is back; a fallback rate above 5% for 10 minutes is the api-cache-fallback-rate alert, and a driver-home or garage-home hit rate (hits / warms) under 30% for 60 minutes over at least 50 warms is the api-prefetch-hit-rate alert

entries.name: motorfix_cache_warm_read_seconds
entries.reason: times each read a warm fills, by kind: a sign-in warm (driver-home, garage-home), the wait a hit on that entry saves, shown as its p75 on the pre-fetch panel, and the post-deploy warm-up (profile, home, popular-brands), which no panel shows

entries.name: motorfix_quote_requests_sent_total
entries.reason: counts quote requests sent by outcome (sent with its recipients, cannot_receive, limit, invalid — invalid counts the use case's own refusals, not the validation pipe's or a missing Idempotency-Key), with one log line per send naming the outcome and the request id; a count has no failure to alert on; the api-error-rate rule covers the service that reports it

entries.name: motorfix_request_received_total
entries.reason: counts each garage a new request reaches by outcome (built, muted, skipped), with one log line per event naming the request id and how many staff it reached; a count has no failure to alert on; the worker-jobs-failed rule covers the service that reports it

entries.name: motorfix_quotes_sent_total
entries.reason: counts quotes garages send by outcome (sent, refused, already_answered, request_not_open; refused covers the service's own 400, 403 and 404, the validation pipe's 400s show in the route metric) and records motorfix_quote_response_minutes (request created to quote sent) with no identifiers, with one Quotes log line per send naming the quote id, the request id and the outcome; a count has no failure to alert on; the api-error-rate rule covers the service that reports it

entries.name: motorfix_quote_accepts_total
entries.reason: counts the acceptances drivers try by outcome (accepted, replayed, booking_pending, slot_passed, invalid_transition, refused; refused covers the service's 404 and the controller's Idempotency-Key 400, the validation pipe's 400s show in the route metric) with no identifiers, with one QuoteAccept log line per try naming the quote id, the booking id and the outcome; a drop in acceptances is a product signal, not an outage; the api-error-rate rule covers the service that reports it

entries.name: motorfix_quote_declines_total
entries.reason: counts the declines drivers try by outcome (declined, invalid_transition, refused; refused covers the service's 404, the validation pipe's 400s show in the route metric) with no identifiers, with one QuoteDecline log line per try naming the quote id and the outcome; a count has no failure to alert on; the api-error-rate rule covers the service that reports it

entries.name: motorfix_request_declines_total
entries.reason: counts garage declines by outcome (declined, already_answered, request_not_open, invalid; invalid counts the service's own 403 and 404, the validation pipe's 400s show in the route metric) and reason code, with no identifiers, and one Declines log line per decline naming the recipient and request ids; the route is POST /api/v1/garage/requests/{id}/decline in http.server.request.duration; a count has no failure to alert on; the api-error-rate rule covers the service that reports it

entries.name: motorfix_decline_windows_closed_total
entries.reason: counts each closed decline undo window by outcome and whether the timer or the sweep closed it; a rising sweep share means lost timers; a count has no failure to alert on; the api-error-rate rule covers the service that reports it

entries.name: motorfix_verification_result_total
entries.reason: an admin's decision through POST /api/v1/admin/verification-files/:id/decision reaches it, as does the automatic approval under APP_ENV=test; counts each verification decision told to its garage's owners by outcome (built, skipped: no owner or no decision to tell), with the fan-out's log line naming the file id; also on motorfix-product; a count has no failure to alert on, the verification-result queue entry owns the final-failure alert

entries.name: motorfix_garage_suspended_notices_total
entries.reason: counts each suspension told to its garage's owners by outcome (built, skipped: no owner or no open suspension), with the fan-out's log line naming the garage id; a count has no failure to alert on, the garage-suspended queue entry owns the failed-job alert

entries.name: motorfix_garage_restored_notices_total
entries.reason: counts each restore told to its garage's owners by outcome (built, skipped: no owner or a bad payload), with the fan-out's log line naming the garage id; also on motorfix-product; a count has no failure to alert on, the garage-restored queue entry owns the failed-job alert

entries.name: motorfix_garage_report_decided_notices_total
entries.reason: counts each report decision told to its reporters by outcome (built, skipped: no garage, an unknown decision or no reporter list), with the fan-out's log line naming the garage id; a count has no failure to alert on, the garage-report-decided queue entry owns the failed-job alert

entries.name: motorfix_garage_suspensions_total
entries.reason: counts each garage suspension by cause (recheck_failed, documents_overdue, admin, report_confirmed); the audit holds who and why; a count has no failure to alert on, the admin-garage-suspension endpoint entry owns the error and latency alerts

entries.name: motorfix_garage_restores_total
entries.reason: counts each suspended garage an admin put back on the map, by the cause lifted; not started at 0, so the API stays under its 150 series; the audit holds who, the evidence and the note; a count has no failure to alert on, the admin-garage-restore endpoint entry owns the error and latency alerts

entries.name: motorfix_rechecks_total
entries.reason: counts each monthly register re-check an admin recorded, by result (ok, failed); the audit holds who, the date checked and the activities; a count has no failure to alert on, the rechecks endpoint entry owns the error and latency alerts

entries.name: motorfix_quote_received_total
entries.reason: counts each sent quote announced to its driver by outcome (built, muted), with the fan-out's log line naming the quote id; also on motorfix-product; a count has no failure to alert on; the worker-jobs-failed rule covers the service that reports it

entries.name: motorfix_review_announced_total
entries.reason: counts each posted review announced to its garage's owners by outcome (built, muted, skipped), with the fan-out's log line naming the review id; a count has no failure to alert on; the worker-jobs-failed rule covers the service that reports it

entries.name: garage-features-set
entries.reason: each change of a switch is audited with the owner, the feature and the old and new state, and recorded as a garage.features_changed event in the same transaction; a 409 mechanics_on_team is the rule working, not a failure

entries.name: garage-mechanics-list
entries.reason: a read with no side effect, so nothing is audited; its request span and log line carry the route and status, and a 404 feature_off or not_found is the access rule working, not a failure

entries.name: garage-members-list
entries.reason: a read of what the database already holds, so nothing is audited and no event is owed; its request span and log line carry the route and status, and a 403 forbidden or 404 not_found is the access rule working, not a failure

entries.name: garage-mechanics-add
entries.reason: each card added is audited (create, the owner as actor) and recorded as mechanic.added in the outbox in the same transaction; a 403 mechanic_owned_field or a 422 validation_failed is the owner's input refused, not a failure

entries.name: garage-mechanics-edit
entries.reason: each changed field is audited (update, old and new value) and recorded as mechanic.updated with the fields; an unchanged save writes nothing; a 404 not_found is a card removed in another tab

entries.name: garage-mechanics-remove
entries.reason: each removal is audited (delete) and recorded as mechanic.removed in the same transaction; the STAFF_REMOVED e-mail and push go through the notifications pipeline, whose sends and failures its own entries count, and a failed send is logged as an error with the card id while the removal stays; a 409 owner_row is the rule working

entries.name: admin-garage-suspension
entries.reason: each suspension and each refused one is audited with the admin, the cause and the reason; the count by cause is the motorfix_garage_suspensions_total entry

entries.name: admin-garage-restore
entries.reason: each restore is audited with the admin, the cause lifted, its evidence and the note, and logged once with the garage, the cause and whether a re-check rode with it (never the note); the count by cause is the motorfix_garage_restores_total entry

entries.name: rechecks
entries.reason: each recorded re-check is audited with the admin, the date checked and the activities before and after, and logged once with the garage and the result

entries.name: admin-report-decision
entries.reason: one log line per decision naming the file id, the decision and the reports closed, never the note or the reason; each decision and each refused one is audited with the admin; the count by outcome is the motorfix_report_decisions_total entry and the refusals are on motorfix_verification_decision_refusals_total; no alert of its own, as the …/:id/decision endpoint: a refusal is the rule working, and the API error-rate and latency rules cover the route

entries.name: admin-catalogue-job-decisions
entries.reason: the queue read and the two decisions; one log line per decision naming the job id, the decision and the admin's account id, never the rejection reason; each decision is audited with the admin; the approvals and rejections are told apart by the route on the request metric, so no product counter of their own; a 409 or 422 is the rule working, and the API error-rate and latency rules cover the routes

entries.name: quote-requests-compare
entries.reason: the driver's comparison of one request's quotes, read from PostgreSQL and writing quote.first_seen_at once; no counter or alert of its own: a read of the driver's own data, covered by the API's error-rate and latency alerts; no outside call

entries.name: quote-requests-active
entries.reason: the driver's own open request and its stage, read from PostgreSQL for the dashboard panel; no counter or alert of its own: a read of the driver's own data, covered by the API's error-rate and latency alerts; no outside call

entries.name: quotes
entries.reason: one log line per send naming the quote id, the request id and the outcome; the send counter and response-time histogram are the motorfix_quotes_sent_total entry

entries.name: quote-accept
entries.reason: one log line per acceptance naming the quote id, the booking id and the outcome; the count by outcome is the motorfix_quote_accepts_total entry

entries.name: quote-decline
entries.reason: one log line per decline naming the quote id and the outcome; the count by outcome is the motorfix_quote_declines_total entry

entries.name: motorfix_searches_total
entries.reason: a count has no failure to alert on; the api-error-rate rule covers the service that reports it

entries.name: motorfix_sort_changes_total
entries.reason: a count has no failure to alert on; a sort change on Results is counted here by sort and never as a search, and every other unlogged first page that names Distanță or Preț (a reload, the Reîncarcă retry, a map settle, a step through the history, the restart after an invalid cursor) counts once more, an overcount accepted in the plan

entries.name: motorfix_search_cache_total
entries.reason: counts each garage search page read by cache outcome (hit, miss, fallback when Redis failed and PostgreSQL answered), with one warn log line when Redis first fails and one when it is back; a fallback rate above 5% for 10 minutes is the api-search-cache-fallback-rate alert

entries.name: motorfix_search_log_total
entries.reason: counts each search log row written or lost, with one warn log line naming the error when a write fails; the search still answers; a failure rate above 5% for 10 minutes is the api-search-log-failure-rate alert

entries.name: motorfix_search_pins_total
entries.reason: counts each pins answer by outcome (results, none) and mode (area, bbox) for the map on Results; a count has no failure to alert on: the route's errors and latency are the api-error-rate and api-latency rules, and its Redis fallback is in motorfix_search_cache_total under the api-search-cache-fallback-rate alert

entries.name: motorfix_similar_garages_total
entries.reason: counts each similar-garages answer for a garage no longer listed by outcome (results, none); a count has no failure to alert on: the route's errors and latency are the api-error-rate and api-latency rules

entries.name: motorfix_sign_ins_total
entries.reason: a count has no failure to alert on; the api-error-rate rule covers the service that reports it

entries.name: motorfix_garage_sign_ups_total
entries.reason: a count has no failure to alert on; the api-error-rate rule covers the service that reports it

entries.name: motorfix_listing_submissions_total
entries.reason: counts each garage listing sent for verification (product action listing_submitted; the consent-gated browser event of the same name keeps firing from the page), charted per hour and per day on motorfix-product; a replayed send is not counted; a count has no failure to alert on; the api-error-rate rule covers the service that reports it

entries.name: motorfix_listing_completions_total
entries.reason: counts each completion copy an owner opens to answer a request for more once per copy: opening the same copy again is not counted; charted beside the requests for more and the files returned on motorfix-product; a count has no failure to alert on; the api-error-rate rule covers the service that reports it

entries.name: motorfix_garage_approvals_total
entries.reason: an admin's decision through POST /api/v1/admin/verification-files/:id/decision reaches it, as does the automatic approval under APP_ENV=test; a count has no failure to alert on; the api-error-rate rule covers the service that reports it

entries.name: motorfix_verification_decision_refusals_total
entries.reason: counts each admin decision or request for more refused by reason (rar_check_required, caen_check_required, note_required, reason_required, note_too_short, already_decided, and for a report decision no_open_report), with the Verification log line naming the file; a refusal is the rule working, not a failure, so it has no alert; the api-error-rate rule covers the service that reports it

entries.name: motorfix_verification_rejections_total
entries.reason: counts each garage verification file rejected, by reason (documents, rar, address, photos, other), with the Verification log line naming the file, the admin and the reason (never the message) and the reason on the request span; more than 5 in an hour fires the burst alert

entries.name: motorfix_verification_reopenings_total
entries.reason: counts each reopened verification file by who reopened it (admin, system); a count has no failure to alert on; the api-error-rate rule covers the service that reports it

entries.name: motorfix_verification_more_requests_total
entries.reason: counts each garage verification file sent back for more details, with the Verification log line naming the file, the admin and the items asked for (never the message) and the items on the request span; more than 5 in an hour fires the burst alert

entries.name: motorfix_verification_resubmissions_total
entries.reason: counts each file a garage sends again after a request for more, with one Verification log line naming the file; a count has no failure to alert on; the api-error-rate rule covers the service that reports it

entries.name: motorfix_quotes_total
entries.reason: a count has no failure to alert on; the api-error-rate rule covers the service that reports it

entries.name: motorfix_emails_sent_total
entries.reason: a count has no failure to alert on; the worker-jobs-failed rule covers the service that reports it

entries.name: motorfix_notifications_sent_total
entries.reason: a count has no failure to alert on; the worker-jobs-failed rule covers the service that reports it

entries.name: admin-account
entries.metric: http.server.request.duration by http.route GET /api/v1/admin/accounts/:id and POST /api/v1/admin/accounts/:id/reset-access, /suspend, /restore and /delete-on-request
entries.reason: each action logs one 'admin account action' line with the account, the admin, the action and its outcome (never a name, e-mail or reason), each refusal one 'admin accounts request failed' line with the :id route; outcomes count on motorfix_admin_account_actions_total; spans come from the HTTP and Prisma auto-instrumentation

entries.name: garage-job-steps
entries.reason: each refusal logs one 'job step refused' line with ids and its code

entries.name: motorfix_job_steps_total
entries.reason: counts step changes by action (added, renamed, reordered, removed, ticked, unticked); a count has no failure to alert on; the api-error-rate rule covers the service that reports it

entries.name: motorfix_account_changes_total
entries.reason: counts saved changes of an account's own details by field (name, city, email, phone, password); a change count has no failure mode of its own

entries.name: my-details
entries.metric: http.server.request.duration by http.route PATCH /api/v1/me, POST /api/v1/me/email, /api/v1/me/phone, /api/v1/me/phone/confirm and /api/v1/auth/confirm-email (the change link)
entries.reason: each refusal logs one 'phone change refused: <code>' or 'e-mail change link not sent' line, never the address or number; the WhatsApp code goes out through the brevo entry and a failed send logs 'phone code not sent: whatsapp_failed (<kind>)' and answers 503 send_failed; saved changes are motorfix_account_changes_total; spans come from the HTTP and Prisma auto-instrumentation

entries.name: auth-password
entries.reason: each refusal logs one 'password change refused: <code>' line and a failed notice e-mail logs 'password changed e-mail not sent'; a saved change counts on motorfix_account_changes_total{field="password"}

entries.name: motorfix_account_deletions_total
entries.reason: counts each request to delete an account by outcome (deleted, forbidden, refused_owner, refused_in_work, reauth_required, mismatch, failed); api-account-deletion-failed fires on any failed deletion

entries.name: motorfix_data_exports_total
entries.reason: counts data exports by outcome: requested, too_soon, already_ready, forbidden and downloaded in the api, ready, failed and expired in the worker; worker-data-export-failed fires on any export failed after its last attempt

entries.name: motorfix_admin_account_actions_total
entries.reason: counts each admin account action (reset_access, suspend, restore, delete_on_request) by outcome (done, refused, conflict, email_failed, failed); api-admin-account-action-failed fires on any failed action

entries.name: auth-account-delete
entries.reason: each refusal logs one 'account deletion refused: <outcome>' line, a deletion logs 'account deleted <id>' and a failed farewell e-mail logs 'account deleted e-mail not sent'; outcomes count on motorfix_account_deletions_total; spans come from the HTTP and Prisma auto-instrumentation

entries.name: me-data-export-request
entries.reason: a request logs 'data export requested <exportId>' and a refusal 'data export refused: <outcome>', ids only; outcomes count on motorfix_data_exports_total; spans come from the HTTP and Prisma auto-instrumentation

entries.name: me-data-export-state
entries.reason: a read of the account's own newest export; an assistant's refusal logs 'data export refused: forbidden'; spans come from the HTTP and Prisma auto-instrumentation

entries.name: me-data-export-download
entries.reason: a download logs 'data export downloaded <exportId>' and counts downloaded on motorfix_data_exports_total; a store failure answers 503 storage_unavailable, counted by api-error-rate; spans come from the HTTP, S3 and Prisma auto-instrumentation

entries.name: garage-reports
entries.reason: refusals show on the request-duration metric by route and status code

entries.name: garage-legal-check
entries.reason: a read only: it changes nothing, so no product counter or audit row; its refusals and latency show on the request-duration metric by route and status code, each refusal writes one LegalCheck warn line with its code and the actor's role, its spans come from the HTTP and Prisma auto-instrumentation, and the API-wide error and latency rules cover it

entries.name: saved-garages
entries.reason: PUT, DELETE, GET ids and the GET list (ST-291) show on the request-duration metric by route and status code; each save and removal is an audit row and a saved_garage.added or saved_garage.removed event, and reading the list changes nothing, so no product counter is added; the list's spans come from the HTTP and Prisma auto-instrumentation

entries.name: motorfix_garage_reports_total
entries.reason: outcomes created, already_reported and refused (both 409); 404 and 429 read from the request-duration metric by route and status; a count has no failure to alert on; the api-error-rate rule covers the service that reports it

entries.name: motorfix_report_decisions_total
entries.reason: an admin's decision through POST /api/v1/admin/verification-files/:id/report-decision reaches it; counts each decision on a garage's open reports by outcome (unfounded, confirmed, confirmed_already_suspended), with the GarageReports log line naming the file; a count has no failure to alert on; the api-error-rate rule covers the service that reports it

entries.name: listing-documents
entries.reason: a page left in storage after a failed delete logs one warning with the draft id and key

entries.name: listing-draft-check
entries.metric: http.server.request.duration by http.route /api/v1/listing-drafts/:id/check and status (200 sendable, 422 listing_incomplete, 404, 409)
entries.reason: read-only and writes nothing; a 422 is the owner's form still lacking values, not a failure, so it is read by status on the dashboard and not alerted on; the api traces carry the route span

entries.name: listing-submit
entries.metric: http.server.request.duration by http.route POST /api/v1/listing-drafts/:id/submit and status (201 sent or replayed, 400 without an Idempotency-Key, 401, 404 draft_not_found, 409 draft_already_submitted or garage_already_exists, 422 validation_failed)
entries.reason: one transaction writes the garage, its owner, the verification file, the outbox rows and the audit entries; each success logs one ListingSubmitService line (draft id, garage id, account id; never an e-mail or a token) and adds to motorfix_listing_submissions_total; no alert of its own: a failed send is a 5xx the api-error-rate rule reads, a refused one is the owner's answer shown on the page, and a replay under the same Idempotency-Key writes nothing; no outside call

entries.name: listing-completion
entries.metric: http.server.request.duration by http.route POST /api/v1/listing-drafts/completion and status (200 the copy, 401, 403 forbidden for staff who are not the owner, 404 not_found with no garage or no file, 409 verification_transition_refused when the file asks for nothing more)
entries.reason: reads the garage into one open copy per file and writes a browser key; the copy's creation logs one Completion line (copy id, file id, garage id; never an e-mail or a token) and adds to motorfix_listing_completions_total; no alert of its own: a failed open is a 5xx the api-error-rate rule reads, a refusal is the page's status view, and a second open answers the same copy; no outside call

entries.name: garage-verification-status
entries.reason: a read with no writes, re-read by the owner's page on each verification event and on reconnect; a 403 or 404 is a caller without access, which the error-rate rule reads with the rest; no counter or alert of its own; no outside call

entries.name: garage-profile
entries.reason: a read with no writes, no event and no audit row, re-read by the owner's profile view on each garage change and on reconnect; it answers through the public profile's cache, so its cache fallbacks count in the API's cache-fallback rule; a 403 is a mechanic or receptionist without the view, a 404 or 410 a garage not shown, which the error-rate rule reads with the rest; its spans come from the HTTP, Prisma and Redis auto-instrumentation; no counter or alert of its own; no outside call

entries.name: admin-verification-documents
entries.reason: each issued address writes one open entry in the history and counts motorfix_documents_opened_total

entries.name: admin-verification-file-read
entries.reason: a read with no writes; the API-wide error and latency rules cover it, so it has no alert of its own

entries.name: admin-verification-file-changes
entries.reason: a read: it writes no entry and counts nothing; the request it answers is counted by motorfix_verification_more_requests_total and the return by motorfix_verification_resubmissions_total

entries.name: admin-verification-file-open
entries.reason: the first opening logs one line (file, admin) and emits verification.opened; the API-wide error and latency rules cover it, so it has no alert of its own

entries.name: admin-verification-check-record
entries.reason: each save logs one VerificationChecks line (file, kind, result, admin; never the detail or the company name), writes an audit entry and emits verification.check_recorded, and is counted by motorfix_verification_checks_total; the API-wide error and latency rules cover it, so it has no alert of its own

entries.name: admin-verification-file-decision
entries.reason: each decision logs one Verification line (file, outcome, admin; never the note), writes its audit entry and the verification.decided outbox row, and is counted by motorfix_garage_approvals_total, a rejection by reason by motorfix_verification_rejections_total, a refusal by motorfix_verification_decision_refusals_total; the API-wide error and latency rules cover it, so it has no alert of its own

entries.name: admin-verification-file-reopen
entries.reason: each reopening logs one Verification line (file, admin), writes its audit entry and the verification.reopened outbox row, and is counted by motorfix_verification_reopenings_total; the API-wide error and latency rules cover it, so it has no alert of its own

entries.name: admin-verification-file-rar-number
entries.reason: each correction logs one line (file, admin; never the number) and writes an audit entry with the old and new number; the API-wide error and latency rules cover it, so it has no alert of its own

entries.name: motorfix_verification_checks_total
entries.reason: counts each check an admin records on a garage's file by kind and result; a refused save is not counted; a count has no failure to alert on; the api-error-rate rule covers the service that reports it

entries.name: motorfix_documents_uploaded_total
entries.reason: counts each confirmed document page by kind (onrc_certificate, rar_authorisation); a count has no failure to alert on; the api-error-rate rule covers the service that reports it

entries.name: motorfix_declarations_signed_total
entries.reason: counts each signed declaration; a count has no failure to alert on; the api-error-rate rule covers the service that reports it

entries.name: motorfix_documents_opened_total
entries.reason: it cannot fire on staging while no web screen calls the document download address; counts each time an admin opens a document page, by kind; a count has no failure to alert on; the api-error-rate rule covers the service that reports it

entries.name: admin-demand
entries.reason: the admin's demand read, counts only; a failed read answers the standard error body and is the api-error-rate rule's

entries.name: admin-system-log
entries.reason: the admin's read of the log, today's entries for the Jurnal panel or any range of the last 90 days for the full log, narrowed by type, severity, source and a text search, fifty a page at most behind an opaque cursor on the indexed time range; a failed read answers the standard error body and is the api-error-rate rule's

entries.name: profile-views
entries.reason: the public profile's beacon; every outcome is the motorfix_profile_views_total entry, which owns the lost-view alert

entries.name: motorfix_profile_views_total
entries.reason: counts each beacon by outcome (accepted, bot, staff, no_key, lost, throttled, not_found) with no garage, address or visitor label; a lost view logs one ProfileViews error line naming the Redis error only

entries.name: motorfix_profile_view_rows_total
entries.reason: counts the daily rows the night writes and the days it logs as gaps, with one ProfileViews log line per day naming the day and the count; a failed night is the profile-views-job-failed alert

entries.name: motorfix_consent_records_total
entries.reason: counts each analytics consent choice stored, by decision; a choice count has no failure mode of its own; the consents endpoint carries the api error-rate and latency rules

entries.name: outage-alerts
entries.reason: Grafana's outage contact point calls it; one Outage log line per alert (service, state, fingerprint, admins, sent), never the token or an address; the uptime checks (infra/observability/uptime/checks.json) and the outage rule watch the services it reports on

entries.name: search-garages
entries.reason: answers from the 60 s Redis cache or PostgreSQL; the cache and log outcomes are the motorfix_search_cache_total and motorfix_search_log_total entries, new searches still count in motorfix_searches_total, and `sort` changes in motorfix_sort_changes_total

entries.name: similar-garages
entries.reason: public read for the no-longer-available view, up to 3 approved garages that work on the brand around a suspended garage, read from PostgreSQL with no cache and no write; answers are counted in motorfix_similar_garages_total; the share button itself makes no server call and is counted through the shared_link profile-view and request sources

entries.name: public-garage-profile
entries.reason: one PostgreSQL statement on a cache miss, the answer cached ten minutes and purged by the garage tag; the cache outcomes are the motorfix_cache_total entry (kind profile)

entries.name: search-garages-pins
entries.reason: every pin of a search for the map on Results, from the 60 s Redis cache or PostgreSQL; its answers count in motorfix_search_pins_total by outcome and mode, and a Redis fallback in motorfix_search_cache_total under the api-search-cache-fallback-rate alert; no outside call (the browser fetches the tiles from the place-step map's provider)

entries.name: maps-static
entries.reason: a public WebP of one map view, cached a day by the browser and a month at the CDN; renders count in motorfix_static_map_renders_total, a refusal past 120 a minute per address in motorfix_rate_limit_refusals_total; one static-map.render span (zoom, theme, size, tile count, never the centre) and one StaticMapRender warning per failed render

entries.name: bunny
entries.reason: the CDN's API, which the worker's CdnPurgeSender calls to purge a garage page (garage:<id>) or the search pages (search) by tag after a cache event; counted by motorfix_cdn_purges_total{outcome=sent|failed}, a failure logs 'cdn purge failed <tag> <status|error>' and the tag goes back on the queue; worker-cdn-purge-failed fires on purges that keep failing for 15 minutes; worker-saturation covers the sender's host, and worker-jobs-failed the relay jobs whose purges it carries. scripts/cdn.ts (release.yml's purge step and the config check) calls the same API from CI, outside the inventory's reach

entries.name: motorfix_cdn_purges_total
entries.reason: counts each tag purge the worker sends to the CDN by outcome (sent, failed); a failed one is queued again and logs one warn line naming the tag and the status

entries.name: motorfix_origin_refused_total
entries.reason: counts each request the web origin refused with 403 because X-Origin-Secret was missing or wrong (someone reaching Railway's address past the CDN), with one warn log line per refusal; no alert: refusals are the lock-down working, and a CDN that stopped sending the secret shows as the web-down and error-rate alerts at the edge

entries.name: support-messages
entries.reason: carries one job per stored contact message (the support e-mail with a reply-to, then the acknowledgement); counted by motorfix_support_emails_total with one Support log line per e-mail naming the reference; the unsent gauge motorfix_support_messages_unsent, read every 60 s, raises support-message-unsent after an hour above 0 (SUPPORT_EMAIL unset or sending failing)

entries.name: motorfix_support_messages_total
entries.reason: counts contact-form sends by outcome (stored, refused_limit, trap, invalid) with no identifiers and one Support log line per stored message naming its reference; a maintenance refusal counts in motorfix_maintenance_refusals_total; a count has no failure to alert on; the api-error-rate rule covers the service that reports it

entries.name: motorfix_support_emails_total
entries.reason: counts the support and acknowledgement e-mails by kind and outcome (sent, blocked, failed, unconfigured); a message left unsent is caught by the gauge's support-message-unsent alert, not by this count

entries.name: motorfix_support_messages_unsent
entries.reason: a gauge of stored messages whose support e-mail is pending or waiting for SUPPORT_EMAIL, read from PostgreSQL every 60 s; above 0 for an hour fires support-message-unsent

entries.name: garage-price-ranges
entries.reason: the owner's in-place change of a job's range and duration, of whether drivers see the job (ST-174, a visible-only body) and of the labour rate, written to PostgreSQL with one audit entry per changed field and a price_list.updated event; a refused or stale save is a 4xx the error-rate rule reads; no counter of its own: an edit is not a product outcome, and the audit holds who changed what; no outside call

entries.name: garage-price-rows
entries.metric: http.server.request.duration by http.route POST /api/v1/garages/:garageId/prices, DELETE /api/v1/garages/:garageId/prices/:priceId, POST /api/v1/garages/:garageId/catalogue-jobs
entries.reason: the owner's add of an approved catalogue job to the price list, the proposal of a job the catalogue lacks (catalogue-jobs.controller.ts: a pending job_type with its catalogue_job.proposed event) and the removal with the job's brand ranges and ticks, written to PostgreSQL with their audit entries and a price_list.updated event in one transaction; a refused add, proposal or removal is a 4xx the error-rate rule reads; no counter of its own: the audit holds who added and proposed what; no outside call

entries.name: booking-timers
entries.reason: carries the relay's quote.accepted and booking.confirmed events and each accepted booking's two confirm reminders and its lapse, with the 5-minute sweep for a lost lapse; one BookingTimers log line per fired timer naming the booking id and what it did; lapses counted by motorfix_booking_lapses_total (request quoted or closed, by timer or sweep); BullMQ's queue metrics cover depth and failures; booking-lapse-sweep-late fires when the sweep lapses more than 10 bookings in an hour (lost timers)

entries.name: booking-confirmed
entries.reason: one log line per job naming the booking id and whether the driver was told; BullMQ's queue metrics cover depth and failures; the confirmations themselves are counted by motorfix_booking_confirms_total

entries.name: booking-lapsed
entries.reason: one log line per job naming the booking id and how many were told, the driver and the garage's owners and receptionists; BullMQ's queue metrics cover depth and failures; the lapses themselves are counted by motorfix_booking_lapses_total

entries.name: motorfix_booking_confirms_total
entries.reason: counts the confirmations garages try by outcome (confirmed, mechanic_busy, lift_busy, outside_hours, mechanic_unavailable, invalid_transition, refused) with no identifiers, with one Confirm log line per try naming the booking id and the outcome; a refusal is a garage's choice, not an outage; the api-error-rate rule covers the service that reports it

entries.name: motorfix_booking_lapses_total
entries.reason: counts each lapsed booking by what became of its request (quoted when another quote is open, closed) and whether the timer or the sweep lapsed it; a rising sweep share means lost timers, which booking-lapse-sweep-late watches

entries.name: account-closed
entries.reason: carries the relay's account.deleted and account.suspended events; one AccountClosed log line per event naming the account id and the requests closed, skipped and failed and the bookings cancelled and skipped; a request that fails is retried with the job (3 tries) and worker-jobs-failed fires on the last; the outcomes are counted by motorfix_account_closed_cleanups_total; BullMQ's queue metrics cover depth and failures

entries.name: data-export
entries.reason: carries the relay's data_export.requested and account.deleted events and the hourly sweep; log lines 'data export <id>: built <n> files, <bytes> bytes', 'failed after 3 attempts: <ErrorClass>', 'account deleted, expired' and 'data export sweep: expired <n>'; a build is retried with the job (3 tries) and counted by motorfix_data_exports_total; BullMQ's queue metrics cover depth and failures

entries.name: car-account-deleted
entries.reason: carries the relay's account.deleted events; one CarAccountDeleted log line per event naming the account id and the plates cleared; a failed job is retried (3 tries) and worker-jobs-failed fires on the last; BullMQ's queue metrics cover depth and failures

entries.name: review-ratings
entries.reason: carries the relay's review events; one ReviewRatings log line per event naming the review id and whether the garage's and the mechanic's figures were written, unchanged or gone, and a warning for a review that no longer exists; a failed recount is retried with the job (3 tries) and worker-jobs-failed fires on the last; BullMQ's queue metrics cover depth and failures

entries.name: request-cancelled
entries.reason: one log line per job naming the request id and how many of the garages' owners and receptionists were told; BullMQ's queue metrics cover depth and failures

entries.name: booking-cancelled
entries.reason: one log line per job naming the booking id and how many were told, the garage's owners and receptionists and the booked mechanic; only a closed driver account's cancellations are sent from here; BullMQ's queue metrics cover depth and failures

entries.name: motorfix_account_closed_cleanups_total
entries.reason: counts each request a closed driver account left open by outcome (closed, skipped because its booking had started, failed) and each booking by outcome (cancelled, skipped); a count has nothing to alert on, and a failed clean-up is the account-closed job failing, which worker-jobs-failed watches

entries.name: booking-confirm
entries.reason: one Confirm log line per try naming the booking id and the outcome; the count by outcome is the motorfix_booking_confirms_total entry

entries.name: booking-confirm-options
entries.reason: a read of the mechanics and lifts a confirmation may pick; it writes nothing, so its failures and latency are the route metric alone

entries.name: review-eligibility
entries.reason: a read of whether the caller may review each of up to 50 jobs; it writes nothing and counts nothing on the review counter, so its failures and latency are the route metric alone

entries.name: mechanic-reviews
entries.reason: a public read of a mechanic's published reviews, 20 a page; it writes nothing, so its failures and latency are the route metric alone

entries.name: garage-reviews
entries.reason: a public read of a garage's published reviews, 20 a page, with its rating, count and breakdown; it writes nothing, so its failures and latency are the route metric alone

entries.name: garage-staff-reviews
entries.reason: the garage owner's and receptionist's read of their own published and reported reviews, 20 a page, with the profile's figures; it writes nothing, so its failures and latency are the route metric alone

entries.name: motorfix_reviews_posted_total
entries.reason: counts each publish a driver tries by outcome (published, job_not_done, own_garage, already_reviewed, review_removed, email_not_confirmed) with no identifiers, with the review's create audit entry and the review.posted event naming the job; a refusal is the driver's state, not an outage; the api-error-rate rule covers the endpoint that reports it

entries.name: owner-legal-documents
entries.reason: each sending counts motorfix_document_cycle_total{step=uploaded}, writes one history entry per document and one document.uploaded event, and tells the admins through ADMIN_VERIFICATION_QUEUED

entries.name: admin-legal-document-decision
entries.reason: each decision counts motorfix_document_cycle_total{step=accepted|refused}, writes its history entry and one document.accepted or document.refused event, with the DocumentReview log line naming the document, its kind, the outcome and the admin's role, never the note

entries.name: motorfix_document_cycle_total
entries.reason: counts each step of the yearly document cycle (reminders, overdue, uploads, acceptances, refusals); a count has no failure to alert on; the api-error-rate and worker-jobs-failed rules cover the services that report it

entries.name: motorfix_retention_rows_total
entries.reason: counts the rows each nightly retention run removed or anonymised, by kind (eight fixed kinds, started at 0 in the worker); panel Retention rows per night; a failed run and a run that has not completed in 48 hours are both worker-jobs-failed's (reason failed or overdue)

entries.name: motorfix_documents_overdue
entries.reason: a gauge of yearly document cycles in the overdue state, refreshed by each run of the compliance step and shown on the Documente anuale panel; a run that fails for good leaves it stale and fires worker-jobs-failed, which covers the reminders queue

entries.name: motorfix_notification_channel_choices_total
entries.reason: a count of channel choices drivers save has no failure to alert on; api-error-rate covers the route that saves them

entries.name: me-acceptance
entries.reason: a signed-in account accepting the terms and privacy notice in force: the missing rows and their audit entry in one transaction, counted by motorfix_acceptances_total, one Acceptance log line without the account id; a 400 consent_required is a stale page sending old versions, the rule working; the API error-rate and latency rules cover the route; no outside call

entries.name: motorfix_acceptances_total
entries.reason: counts every acceptance that wrote a row after a version change, never an account; a count has no failure of its own to alert on, a failed write is a 5xx under api-error-rate

entries.name: motorfix_consent_refusals_total
entries.reason: counts every call refused with consent_required by surface api or mcp, never an account; a surge right after a version bump is the expected shape, not a failure, so it is watched on the panel, not paged
